messages.author: 5e9201f19b3ebb4b
messages.subject: Error while sampling
parts:
Hello,
I've been trying to convert some BUGS scripts to STAN, with some
success. However, sometimes (1/3 of chains) displays an error message
in each iteration of the chain:

Warning (non-fatal rejection): Error in function
stan::prob::normal_log<N4stan5agrad3varE>(N4stan5agrad3varE): Random
variate y is 1.#QNAN:0, but must not be nan!

The sampled chains end up with n_eff = 1. Is this a bug, or did I mess
something up? Here's the code for the model:

data {
int<lower=1> k; # number of subjects
int<lower=0> h[k]; # Hits
int<lower=0> f[k]; # False Alarms
int<lower=1> n; # False Alarms + correct rejections
int<lower=1> s; # Hits + misses
}

parameters {
real<lower=-5,upper=5> muc; # mean bias
real<lower=-5,upper=5> mud; # mean discriminability
real<lower=0> sigmac; # sd bias
real<lower=0> sigmad; # sd discriminability
real<lower=0> c[k];
real<lower=0> d[k];

}

model {

#Priors
muc ~ normal(0,100);
mud ~ normal(0,100);
sigmac ~ uniform(0,10);
sigmad ~ uniform(0,10);
c ~ normal(muc,sigmac);
d ~ normal(mud,sigmad);
for (i in 1:k) {
h[i] ~ binomial(s,Phi(d[i]/2-c[i]));
f[i] ~ binomial(n,Phi(-d[i]/2-c[i]));
}
}

Cheers,
Marcel

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Error while sampling
parts:
On 9/15/12 11:00 AM, Marcel Falkiewicz wrote:
> Hello,
> I've been trying to convert some BUGS scripts to STAN, with some
> success. However, sometimes (1/3 of chains) displays an error message
> in each iteration of the chain:

Are the other chains giving you similar answers
to BUGS?

> Warning (non-fatal rejection): Error in function
> stan::prob::normal_log<N4stan5agrad3varE>(N4stan5agrad3varE): Random
> variate y is 1.#QNAN:0, but must not be nan!

We changed the error messages for 1.0.2, so
they won't mention variates not in the model.

What this means is the variate parameter in
a log sampling statement went awry. You
have two classes of these:

> muc ~ normal(0,100);
> mud ~ normal(0,100);

> c ~ normal(muc,sigmac);
> d ~ normal(mud,sigmad);

so it's either muc, mud, c, or d. (We're trying
to figure out how to get better line-by-line
debugging in without too much computational overhead
-- sorry for the current cryptic error messages.)

Are you specifying initial values or letting Stan
do it?
> The sampled chains end up with n_eff = 1.

You run multiple chains and together every parameter
has n_eff = 1? That sounds like it may be some
kind of boundary condition computation if things
aren't moving.

There's also problem in your model with
the variable declarations. Every variable needs
to be constrained to its support.

When you declare

> parameters {
> ...

> real<lower=0> sigmac; # sd bias
> real<lower=0> sigmad; # sd discriminability

you are saying the support is (0,+infinity), which
contradicts the sampling statement:

> model {
...

> sigmac ~ uniform(0,10);
> sigmad ~ uniform(0,10);

which says the support is (0,10).

Could you try it again with matching declarations and
see if the problem goes away?

If there's still a problem, could you also send us
the data you're running that's problematic (feel
free to use e-mail: st...@mc-stan.org.

There might also be numerical issues in Phi().
We've gotten around some of these in the logit case
by writing a logit-parameterized density function
directly (just for bernoulli, but we'll add binomial).

- Bob
